analysis.investment_thesis: Cyient is a competent engineering services company with a clean balance sheet, but its 23.28% promoter holding is too low for my confidence, the sector is outside my circle, and recent operating income actually declined from INR 1,303 Cr to INR 1,138 Cr in FY25 — a wrong-direction move for a business priced at 19x earnings.
key_strengths: Very conservative balance sheet — D/E of only 0.07 with net cash position (cash INR 1,067 Cr vs debt INR 513 Cr in FY25)
Reasonable trailing P/E of 19x and attractive forward P/E of 14.6x — the market is not demanding an excessive premium
Free cash flow has been consistently positive (INR 688 Cr in FY25) and operating cash flow positive all 5 years
key_risks: Promoter holding at just 23.28% is very low — I cannot invest confidently in a business where founders/promoters have so little skin in the game
ROE of only 12.8% is below my 15% minimum; the business is not earning adequate returns on the capital it holds
Operating income and EBITDA both declined in FY25 vs FY24 despite revenue growing — margin pressure is an early warning sign
red_flags: Finance costs have grown at 21.6% CAGR over 9 years while net profit CAGR was only 8.2% — leverage creeping up faster than earnings
Other income has collapsed from INR 112-158 Cr range (2016-2021) to near-zero, meaning headline PAT quality has been suppressed — the underlying business earns less than it appeared
Engineering services IT is highly dependent on discretionary client budgets in aerospace, defence, and telecom — cyclical revenue with limited pricing power
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Cyient is not a bad business, but it is not the kind of business I build conviction in. Engineering services for aerospace and defence clients requires deep technical relationships, which creates some stickiness, but the demand is discretionary and lumpy. The 9-year revenue CAGR of 10% and net profit CAGR of 8.2% tell a story of steady but unremarkable progress. More worrying, FY25 saw EBITDA and operating income decline despite revenue growth — suggesting the business is running harder to stand still on profitability.

The critical disqualifier for me is the 23.28% promoter holding. I need to see a promoter with their wealth concentrated in the business — that alignment creates discipline and focus. With institutional investors holding the majority, short-term pressures tend to dominate. Unless promoter holding were to increase materially, I would not build a position here regardless of valuation.
